source: NCERT Class XII, Fundamentals of Human Geography, Ch. 2 (The World Population: Distribution, Density and Growth).

sections.heading: 1. Distribution and Density
points: **Population distribution** = how people are spread over the earth; very **uneven** — ~90% live in ~10% of the land.
**Population density** = number of people per unit area (persons/sq km).
Factors: **geographical (water, landforms, climate, soil), economic (minerals, industry, urbanisation), and social/cultural (religion, politics)**.
Dense: South/East Asia, Europe, NE USA; sparse: deserts, poles, high mountains, dense forests.

sections.heading: 2. Population Growth
points: **Growth of population** = change in the number of people over time; **growth rate** (%) — natural (births − deaths) + migration.
**Birth rate, death rate, and natural increase** determine growth.
World population grew slowly until the Industrial Revolution, then **exploded** ('population explosion') due to falling death rates.
**Doubling time** — the time for a population to double.

sections.heading: 3. Demographic Transition Theory
points: The **Demographic Transition Theory** describes population change in stages as a society develops:

sub: **Stage 1:** high birth AND high death rates → low, stable population.
**Stage 2:** high birth, falling death rates → rapid growth (population explosion).
**Stage 3:** falling birth and death rates → growth slows and stabilises.

points: Developed countries are in the later stages; many developing countries in stage 2/3.

sections.heading: 4. Population Control
points: **Overpopulation** strains resources; **population control** via family planning, education (especially women's), health care.
**Thomas Malthus** warned population grows faster (geometrically) than food (arithmetically) → checks.
Balanced population and resources are key to sustainable development.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Population distribution is very uneven (~90% in ~10% of land).
Density = persons per sq km; growth = natural increase + migration.
Demographic Transition: Stage 1 (high birth/death), Stage 2 (explosion), Stage 3 (stable).
Malthus: population grows geometrically, food arithmetically.
Population control: family planning, women's education, health care.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Stage 2 of demographic transition = population explosion** (high birth, falling death).
**Density = persons per unit area**; distribution = the spread/pattern.
**Malthus** linked population growth (geometric) to food (arithmetic).
Population growth = **natural increase (births − deaths) + migration**.
